hero.name: Jeshin
hero.tagline: From a from-scratch web server to backend services, infrastructure, and AI — I build things end to end and see them through.

about.label: ABOUT ME
about.body: I'm a backend developer who treats code as a way to solve problems, not just to compute answers. That conviction began with a class project modeling electric-vehicle versus combustion-engine dynamics in MATLAB, grew through a year of measuring and validating composite-material data as an undergraduate researcher, and took shape at 42Seoul, where I learned C/C++ systems programming and how verifying things at the root makes a team stronger. I've since worked across web servers, backend services, infrastructure, and AI.

backend.title: BACKEND DEVELOPER
backend.subtitle: Designing & building server-side systems
backend.body: REST APIs with FastAPI, Express, and Spring, RBAC and JWT auth, and data modeling across RDS, DynamoDB, and S3. I care about secure, well-tested server code — down to building a web server from scratch.

infra.title: INFRA, SECURITY & AI
infra.subtitle: Shipping, securing, and operating services
infra.body: Containerizing with Docker, provisioning AWS with Terraform, CI/CD with GitHub Actions and Jenkins, automation with Ansible — plus security assessments and grounded LLM/RAG pipelines.

now.label: NOW
now.heading: Building & job hunting
now.body: Sharpening my backend skills through projects while preparing to join a strong engineering team.

2025.heading: Hands-on projects
2025.body: Built a security-hardened collaboration platform, automated infrastructure security assessments, and ran a red-team pentest on a legacy e-commerce service — spanning backend, cloud, security, and AI.

2024.heading: 42Seoul
2024.body: Learned C/C++ systems programming project-first, including a from-scratch web server, and grew through peer-to-peer code review and collaboration.

2023.heading: Undergraduate research
2023.body: Spent a year measuring and validating composite-material data as an undergraduate researcher — where verifying with data, rather than trusting given values, became my default.
